messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] processing nhanes data
parts:
Dear Dan,

I am trying to process the NHANES accelerometry data sets using GGIR

  1. ​Can you specify which NHANES accelerometry data set, as many have been released over the years. GGIR has been tested with standard ActiGraph output and not custom unique file formats generated for specific studies. If I am not mistaken the latest NHANES data comes with custom file formats. So, if that is the case then it may be good to better understand how this differs from the standard formats.


  1. Which GGIR version are you working with? In the latest CRAN version we made some enhancements to handle the specific nature of Actigraph files with idle sleep. Although, that would of course only work with standard ActiGraph file formats.

  1. Are you trying to process the csv file or the gt3x file? If csv, can you process the gt3x file?

Thanks, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

"temperature")

Thanks in advance,

messages.author: 8d6b29dd7851ba43
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] processing nhanes data
parts:
Dear Dr. van Hees,

Thank you for your reply. I was able to uncover the source of the issue and will detail below for those interested.
 
1) I am working with the PAX G (https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/pax_g/) and PAX H (https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/pax_h/) raw (80hz) data (2011-2014).  These are stored in ~14000 compressed folders (1 per individual) and further divided into 1 hour long CSVs. Therein lies the issue I was having with processing part 1. Because each csv only covers 1 hour, the default windowsizes settings are too large to process. It is possible to get around this by setting windowsizes = c(5,600,600). However, I would not recommend this since the summary files for Part 2 and beyond would not be created due to insufficient time (only 1 hour per file!). Instead it is best to extract and combine the data into a single csv, then process with GGIR.

2) I am using GGIR_2.4-0. Since the original post I have been able to successfully process some of the data using the above code and am working to get time on a cluster to process the rest. 

3) Unfortunately, NHANES does not provide the gt3x files as far as I know. 

Thanks again,
Dan
